title: How an LLM picks the next word
objective: Learners see how an LLM turns scores into probabilities over candidate next words, and how temperature and top-p change which words can be picked.

recommended.why: A bar chart shows exact probabilities for every candidate word and how temperature and top-p reshape them, step by step.

alternative.why: A probability chart versus a step-by-step story: which makes temperature intuitive?

assumptions: Simplified illustration: the 12 candidate words and their scores are made up, not taken from a real model
Real models score tens of thousands of tokens, and a token is often part of a word
Temperature divides every score before softmax; top-p keeps the smallest set of most likely words whose probabilities reach top-p
The random draw uses a fixed seed, so the same settings always pick the same word
checkDescription: Probabilities add up to 1, the kept set is the smallest group of most likely words whose mass reaches top-p, a lower temperature gives the top word a higher probability, and the picked word is in the kept set.

learnerPrompts.predict: If you raise the temperature to 1.5, will more or fewer words survive the top-p cut? Why?
learnerPrompts.explain: Set temperature to 0.1. Why does top-p stop mattering, and why might a support chatbot still want some randomness?
